args.title: Game carries out its actions
args.description:
The application calls these methods on Game by exactly these names and keyword arguments. Each one changes the object as described.
- Field `status` holds exactly one of: "ready" (New game, no cell revealed yet, timer not started, mine layout not fixed.); "in_progress" (First reveal has happened and the session has not ended.); "won" (Every non-mine cell has been revealed; terminal.); "lost" (A mine was revealed; terminal.)
- Field `difficulty` holds exactly one of: "Beginner" (9 rows by 9 columns with 10 mines.); "Intermediate" (16 rows by 16 columns with 40 mines.); "Expert" (16 rows by 30 columns with 99 mines.)
- Field `cells[].state` holds exactly one of: "hidden" (Cell not yet revealed and not flagged; default state.); "revealed" (Cell has been opened; shows a mine or an adjacency count.); "flagged" (Player marked the hidden cell as a suspected mine.)
- A refusal raises `InvalidActionError` when An action is attempted that the rules do not allow, such as flagging or revealing after the game has been won or lost, revealing a flagged or revealed cell, or a position outside the board; the board and session are left unchanged.
args.given_when_then: Given a Game in a state where the action is allowed (arrange that by setting its fields). When a Game is created with only its required fields and nothing is called on it Then id set to the given identifier; difficulty "Beginner"; status "ready"; started_at null; ended_at null; elapsed_seconds 0; mine_count 10; flag_count 0; cells is an empty list until the first reveal lays out the board; events empty. When `start_game(difficulty)` is called with valid values Then Discards any current board and timer and sets up a new board for the chosen difficulty (Beginner, Intermediate or Expert) with rows, columns and mine_count taken from that difficulty, status ready, elapsed_seconds 0, flag_count 0, no started_at or ended_at, and no mine layout fixed yet; allowed in any status, and the object's fields show it afterwards. When `reveal_cell(row, column)` is called with valid values Then On the first reveal of a ready game, places mines avoiding the target cell and its neighbours, sets started_at, and moves the game to in_progress; then reveals the hidden, unflagged target cell, expanding zero-count regions, and may end the game as lost (on a mine) or won (when all safe cells are revealed); ignored if the game is won or lost, the position is outside the board, or the cell is already revealed or flagged, and the object's fields show it afterwards. When `toggle_flag(row, column)` is called with valid values Then Cycles a hidden cell to flagged (flag_count increases by one) or a flagged cell back to hidden (flag_count decreases by one), without starting the timer; allowed only while the game is ready or in_progress, and ignored for revealed cells or positions outside the board, and the object's fields show it afterwards. One test function per method.

actions.name: start_game
actions.description: Discards any current board and timer and sets up a new board for the chosen difficulty (Beginner, Intermediate or Expert) with rows, columns and mine_count taken from that difficulty, status ready, elapsed_seconds 0, flag_count 0, no started_at or ended_at, and no mine layout fixed yet; allowed in any status.

actions.name: reveal_cell
actions.description: On the first reveal of a ready game, places mines avoiding the target cell and its neighbours, sets started_at, and moves the game to in_progress; then reveals the hidden, unflagged target cell, expanding zero-count regions, and may end the game as lost (on a mine) or won (when all safe cells are revealed); ignored if the game is won or lost, the position is outside the board, or the cell is already revealed or flagged.

actions.name: toggle_flag
actions.description: Cycles a hidden cell to flagged (flag_count increases by one) or a flagged cell back to hidden (flag_count decreases by one), without starting the timer; allowed only while the game is ready or in_progress, and ignored for revealed cells or positions outside the board.

starting_states.description: id set to the given identifier; difficulty "Beginner"; status "ready"; started_at null; ended_at null; elapsed_seconds 0; mine_count 10; flag_count 0; cells is an empty list until the first reveal lays out the board; events empty.

values.meaning: New game, no cell revealed yet, timer not started, mine layout not fixed.
First reveal has happened and the session has not ended.
Every non-mine cell has been revealed; terminal.

rejections.raised_when: An action is attempted that the rules do not allow, such as flagging or revealing after the game has been won or lost, revealing a flagged or revealed cell, or a position outside the board; the board and session are left unchanged.

deck.title: Adjacency count
deck.description: Each safe cell shows the number of mines among its up to eight neighbours.
deck.given_when_then: Given a game with mines placed and a safe cell at a position When the mine layout is fixed Then the cell's adjacent_mine_count equals the number of mines in its up to eight neighbouring cells.

deck.title: Zero expansion
deck.description: A revealed cell with count 0 reveals all neighbours, recursively.
deck.given_when_then: Given a hidden cell with adjacent_mine_count 0 in an in-progress game When the player reveals it Then all its neighbouring hidden cells are revealed and any neighbour with count 0 continues the expansion recursively.

deck.title: Zero expansion stops at numbered cells
deck.description: Expansion does not reveal past cells with a non-zero count, and does not reveal flagged cells.
deck.given_when_then: Given a zero-count reveal that reaches a neighbour with count greater than 0 or a flagged neighbour When expansion runs Then that neighbour is revealed only if hidden and not flagged, and expansion does not continue beyond it.

deck.title: First-click safety
deck.description: The first reveal is never a mine, and its neighbours are mine-free; the layout is fixed at that moment.
deck.given_when_then: Given a game in ready status When the first cell is revealed Then mines are placed so that the revealed cell and all its neighbours have has_mine false, and the layout is fixed.

deck.title: Flag placement on hidden cells
deck.description: Flags may be placed only on hidden cells.
deck.given_when_then: Given an in-progress game and a hidden cell When the player flags it Then the cell state becomes flagged and flag_count increases by one; Given a revealed cell When the player flags it Then the board is unchanged.

deck.title: Flag removal
deck.description: Flags may be removed at any time while in progress; flagged cells cannot be revealed.
deck.given_when_then: Given a flagged cell in an in-progress game When the player removes the flag Then the cell returns to hidden and flag_count decreases by one; Given a flagged cell When the player attempts to reveal it Then the cell remains flagged and is not revealed.

deck.title: Right-click cycle
deck.description: Right-click cycles hidden to flagged to hidden; question marks are not included.
deck.given_when_then: Given a hidden cell When the player right-clicks it Then it becomes flagged; Given a flagged cell When the player right-clicks it Then it becomes hidden; Given a revealed cell When right-clicked Then it is unchanged.

deck.title: Mine counter may go negative
deck.description: Mine counter shows total mines minus flags placed and may be negative.
deck.given_when_then: Given a game with mine_count M and flag_count F When the counter is displayed Then it shows M minus F, including negative values when F exceeds M.

deck.title: Loss on mine reveal
deck.description: Revealing a mine ends the session as lost; all mines are shown and wrong flags are marked.
deck.given_when_then: Given an in-progress game When the player reveals a mine Then status becomes lost, ended_at is set, all mine cells are shown as revealed, and flagged cells without mines are marked as wrong.

deck.title: Win on all safe cells revealed
deck.description: Session is won when every non-mine cell is revealed; remaining unrevealed mines are auto-flagged.
deck.given_when_then: Given an in-progress game When the last non-mine cell is revealed Then status becomes won, ended_at is set, and every unrevealed mine cell becomes flagged.

deck.title: Terminal state rejects changes
deck.description: No reveal or flag changes are accepted after won or lost; only restart is allowed.
deck.given_when_then: Given a game in won or lost status When the player reveals or flags any cell Then the board and status are unchanged; When the player restarts Then a new game is created.

deck.title: Timer starts on first reveal
deck.description: Timer starts on first reveal, not before.
deck.given_when_then: Given a game in ready status When the first cell is revealed Then started_at is set and elapsed time begins; Given a game in ready status When a flag is placed Then the timer does not start.

deck.title: Timer stops at session end
deck.description: Timer stops at win or loss.
deck.given_when_then: Given an in-progress game When the session is won or lost Then elapsed_seconds is fixed at the value at that moment and no longer increases.

deck.title: Timer display cap
deck.description: Timer is capped at 999 seconds for display.
deck.given_when_then: Given elapsed time greater than 999 seconds When the timer is displayed Then it shows 999.

deck.title: Invalid operations ignored
deck.description: Acting on revealed cells, after game end, or outside the board is ignored without changing state.
deck.given_when_then: Given any game state When the player reveals a revealed cell, acts after game end, or targets a position outside the board Then the board and session state are unchanged.

deck.title: Restart resets session
deck.description: Starting a new game discards the current board and timer and returns to ready.
deck.given_when_then: Given a game in any status When the player starts a new game at a chosen difficulty Then a new board is created with status ready, elapsed time zero, and no mine layout fixed.

deck.title: Difficulty grid and mine count
deck.description: Three difficulties define board size and mine count.
deck.given_when_then: Given a player starting a game When Beginner is chosen Then the board is 9x9 with 10 mines; Intermediate yields 16x16 with 40 mines; Expert yields 30x16 with 99 mines.

deck.title: Board edge boundaries
deck.description: Neighbour computation at board edges and corners counts only in-board cells.
deck.given_when_then: Given a cell on the board edge or corner When adjacency is computed Then only neighbours inside the board are counted, giving fewer than eight neighbours.

deck.title: Grid cell presentation
deck.description: Board looks like classic Minesweeper: raised grey hidden tiles, flat light grey revealed tiles, numbers coloured as original (1 blue, 2 green, 3 red).
deck.given_when_then: Given a revealed cell with count 1 When the board is rendered Then the tile is flat light grey and the number is blue.

deck.title: Flag and header presentation
deck.description: Flags render red; the header shows mine counter, timer, and a restart control.
deck.given_when_then: Given a flagged cell When rendered Then a red flag is shown; Given a game in progress When the header is rendered Then mine counter, timer and restart button are visible above the grid.

SPEC-ACT-GAME.test_source:
import pytest

from src.domain.game import Game


STARTED = "2024-01-01T10:00:00+00:00"


def _blank_board(rows, columns, cell_state="hidden", id_prefix="c"):
    """One hidden cell per position, every key the class describes, no mines."""
    return [
        {
            "id": f"{id_prefix}{r}-{c}",
            "row": r,
            "column": c,
            "has_mine": False,
            "adjacent_mine_count": 0,
            "state": cell_state,
        }
        for r in range(rows)
        for c in range(columns)
    ]


def _cell_at(game, row, column):
    matches = [c for c in game.cells if c["row"] == row and c["column"] == column]
    assert len(matches) == 1
    return matches[0]


def test_new_game_has_default_fields():
    # Given: a Game built with only its required field id.
    # When: nothing is called on it.
    game = Game(id="game-1")

    # Then: the documented defaults hold for a newly created game.
    # id was given at construction; defaults come from the class declaration.
    assert game.id == "game-1"
    assert game.difficulty == "Beginner"
    assert game.status == "ready"
    assert game.started_at is None
    assert game.ended_at is None
    assert game.elapsed_seconds == 0
    assert game.mine_count == 10
    assert game.flag_count == 0
    # No reveal has happened, so no board has been laid out yet.
    assert game.cells == []
    assert game.events == []


def test_start_game_discards_old_session_and_sets_up_intermediate_board():
    # Given: an in-progress-looking old session that is actually won, with a
    # timer that ran for 42 seconds, 3 flags placed, and an old board of 81
    # cells where some are revealed and some flagged.
    # The status is "won" (terminal), which start_game is allowed to override
    # because it is allowed in any status.
    game = Game(id="game-2")
    game.difficulty = "Beginner"
    game.status = "won"
    game.started_at = STARTED
    game.ended_at = "2024-01-01T10:00:42+00:00"
    game.elapsed_seconds = 42
    game.mine_count = 10
    game.flag_count = 3
    old_cells = _blank_board(9, 9, id_prefix="old")
    old_cells[0]["state"] = "revealed"
    old_cells[1]["state"] = "flagged"
    game.cells = old_cells

    # When: a new game is started at Intermediate.
    game.start_game(difficulty="Intermediate")

    # Then: the object shows the fresh Intermediate session (16 x 16, 40 mines).
    # Status returns to ready: no reveal has happened yet.
    # Timer is reset: no started_at, no ended_at, elapsed 0.
    # Flags are cleared: flag_count 0.
    # No mine layout is fixed yet, so no cell holds a mine.
    assert game.difficulty == "Intermediate"
    assert game.status == "ready"
    assert game.started_at is None
    assert game.ended_at is None
    assert game.elapsed_seconds == 0
    assert game.mine_count == 40
    assert game.flag_count == 0
    # The old board's cells are discarded: none of its ids remain.
    assert all(not c["id"].startswith("old") for c in game.cells)
    # Every remaining cell is a fresh hidden cell with no mine.
    assert all(c["state"] == "hidden" for c in game.cells)
    assert all(c["has_mine"] is False for c in game.cells)


def test_reveal_cell_on_ready_game_lays_out_board_and_starts_session():
    # Given: a ready Beginner game (9 x 9, 10 mines) with no board yet.
    # Its status is ready, timer not started, cells empty.
    game = Game(id="game-3")
    game.difficulty = "Beginner"
    game.status = "ready"
    game.mine_count = 10
    game.flag_count = 0
    game.cells = []

    # When: the first reveal is made at the corner (0, 0).
    game.reveal_cell(row=0, column=0)

    # Then: the board is laid out as 9 x 9 = 81 cells.
    assert len(game.cells) == 81
    # Exactly the Beginner mine count is placed.
    assert sum(1 for c in game.cells if c["has_mine"]) == 10
    # First-click safety: the target and its in-board neighbours (0,1), (1,0),
    # (1,1) hold no mine, so the first reveal cannot lose.
    for r, c in [(0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1)]:
        assert _cell_at(game, r, c)["has_mine"] is False
    # The target was hidden and unflagged, so it is now revealed.
    assert _cell_at(game, 0, 0)["state"] == "revealed"
    # The first reveal started the timer and moved the game to in_progress.
    # The mine is not hit and not all 71 safe cells are opened by one reveal,
    # so the game is neither lost nor won.
    assert game.started_at is not None
    assert game.ended_at is None
    assert game.status == "in_progress"


def test_toggle_flag_cycles_hidden_to_flagged_and_back_without_starting_timer():
    # Given: an in-progress Beginner game (9 x 9, 10 mines) whose timer was
    # started earlier at STARTED and has run for 0 seconds in this model.
    # All 81 cells are hidden with no mine placed in the target area,
    # so flagging (4, 4) is decided by the flag rule alone.
    game = Game(id="game-4")
    game.difficulty = "Beginner"
    game.status = "in_progress"
    game.started_at = STARTED
    game.elapsed_seconds = 0
    game.mine_count = 10
    game.flag_count = 0
    game.cells = _blank_board(9, 9)

    # When: the hidden cell (4, 4) is toggled once.
    game.toggle_flag(row=4, column=4)

    # Then: the cell becomes flagged and flag_count goes from 0 to 1.
    # The timer is untouched: started_at and elapsed_seconds are as before,
    # and the status is still in_progress.
    assert _cell_at(game, 4, 4)["state"] == "flagged"
    assert game.flag_count == 1
    assert game.started_at == STARTED
    assert game.elapsed_seconds == 0
    assert game.status == "in_progress"

    # When: the same cell is toggled again.
    game.toggle_flag(row=4, column=4)

    # Then: the flagged cell returns to hidden and flag_count returns to 0.
    assert _cell_at(game, 4, 4)["state"] == "hidden"
    assert game.flag_count == 0
    assert game.started_at == STARTED
    assert game.elapsed_seconds == 0
    assert game.status == "in_progress"
